news.title: China's Tech Capital Bans Horns, Grounds Delivery Drones For APEC Summit
news.text: China's freewheeling tech capital of Shenzhen has embraced an unusual quiet as it prepares to host world leaders this week, with car horns banned, delivery drones grounded and residents urged to leave vehicles at home.The meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, which Presidents Donald Trump of the US and Vladimir Putin of Russia will attend, is a chance for Shenzhen to show off its transformation from an agricultural backwater into the high-tech - and orderly, officials hope to show - city it is today. More than 1.5 million local car owners have pledged to stay off the roads in exchange for APEC car stickers and, if they keep their word, transit cards worth up to 100 yuan ($15). From Tuesday, cars with out-of-town plates will be barred from most city districts during the day, Shenzhen traffic police said.Even the city's ubiquitous e-bike riders have been asked to dismount in return for discounts on insurance, while parked bikes are being removed from main streets. Many downtown areas have been spruced up for the summit. READ | First Ever US-China-Russia Trilateral Summit On ThursdayThe venue stands beside Honey Lake, or Xiangmihu, which was home to one of Asia's largest amusement parks when it opened in 1985. The park's long-disused roller coaster was torn down in 2024 to make way for a financial district.Today the lakeside area is lined with fresh flower beds and newly paved roads. Not everyone in Shenzhen seems ready for all the pomp, and inconvenience, involved with having around 20 world leaders and their entourages descend on the city, however."It's pretty, but that's my taxpayer money they're spending," said Beau, in her 40s, who lives near the venue. She declined to use her full name because her employer had told staff not to speak to media.She will not be able to drive to work this week as nearby roads will be closed at key times, she said.Beau said her bigger headache is childcare. Shenzhen's primary and middle schools begin a four-day autumn break on Tuesday. Except teachers, there is no holiday for adults.Shenzhen has encouraged employers to allow remote work, staggered hours or paid leave. Some residents are making the most of it. John, a middle-school teacher, is heading to the southwestern city of Chongqing. "I just want to relax and enjoy cheap food, and come back when things are back to normal," he said. On the roads, the hush owes much to a citywide ban on beeping that came in this month, enforced by acoustic cameras and fines starting at 300 yuan. Shenzhen has long restricted horn use, but the new rules have been widely publicized. "People are cutting in much more dangerously, you've just got to sit and watch," complained Liu, a 29-year-old working in media, on the ban on using her car horn. READ | How China's Delivery Robots Are Learning To Tackle Night ShiftsDrones, one of the city's most famous exports, have been grounded, with Meituan suspending drone deliveries for 10 days.Preparations extend to wardrobes. An office worker called Lin said her employer had told staff not to wear clothing printed with English phrases they did not understand, in case they were inadvertently displaying obscenities.Still, across the city, tens of thousands of people are wearing red jackets with "volunteer" written on them, including security guards at housing compounds. "My boss told me we have to wear them," said Guo, a guard in Shenzhen's Nanshan district, adding that he didn't understand the letters. "I don't speak English," he explained.(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)
news.summary: Even the city's ubiquitous e-bike riders have been asked to dismount in return for discounts on insurance, while parked bikes are being removed from main streets.
news.author: Reuters

news.title: Dan Sullivan Breaks Silence as Alaska Senate Race Nears Showdown
news.text: For nearly two weeks, as Alaska counted its ballots one batch at a time, Senator Dan Sullivan's campaign said little in public about the race that will decide whether he keeps his seat. On Monday afternoon, it spoke, briefly and carefully, and with a promise attached. "The campaign will have more to say by the end of this week," spokesman Nate Adams said in a statement posted to the campaign's Facebook page. The statement said the campaign would "let that process run its course until every legal vote is counted and certified," and that it would not be "commenting on individual ballot updates or outside projections in the meantime." "The Division of Elections has work left to do, and we respect the Alaskans doing it," the statement added. It also struck a note of thanks: "Senator Sullivan is grateful to the Alaskans who made their voices heard, and he remains focused on his work for our state." It was the first post on the race from either of Sullivan's Facebook accounts since election night. The campaign page had last posted on November 3, a livestream of the senator's remarks. In the days since, his official Senate page posted two tributes, one marking the Marine Corps' 251st birthday and one for Veterans Day, and nothing on the race. Alaska Senate Race Results: Where Mary Peltola and Dan Sullivan Stand Democrat Mary Peltola leads. The Division of Elections' latest unofficial results show Peltola with 141,637 first-choice votes, or 49.98 percent, and Sullivan with 130,162, or 45.93 percent. Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., a retired teacher from Petersburg who shares the senator's name, has 4,684. Those figures were correct as of publication. As of 9:52 p.m. ET Monday, the Associated Press (AP) estimated that 98 percent of votes had been counted, and it had not called the race. The news agency says it declares a winner only when there is "no scenario that would allow the trailing candidate to close the gap." A Newsweek analysis of the elections division figures shows Peltola is 52 votes shy of a majority of the votes counted so far in the race. That figure reflects the current standings and will change as more ballots are counted, because each new ballot also raises the number needed for a majority. Under Alaska's system, a candidate who wins more than half of first-choice votes is elected outright. Otherwise the last-place finisher is eliminated, and those ballots move to voters' next choices, round by round. Peltola's campaign said late Friday that Sullivan has "no mathematical path" to victory. Sullivan's campaign once projected the opposite. A November 4 memo said that if the ranked-choice tabulation were run on the ballots then in hand, "Senator Dan Sullivan would defeat Mary Peltola 105,037 to 104,709, a margin of 328 votes." A follow-up memo on November 6 stood by that call, saying Sullivan "wins by about 320." Both memos worked from a count in which Peltola led on first choices by 626 votes. The second memo also set a test for the early and absentee ballots still to come: "If Peltola's first-choice lead is under about 1,100 once those are in, Sullivan is on track to win the tabulation." On the elections division's latest count, her first-choice lead is 11,475 votes. Measured against the campaign's own benchmark, that gap is the backdrop for Monday's promise to say more by week's end. Dan Sullivan, Mary Peltola and the Fight Over a Second Dan Sullivan Monday's measured language stands apart from the campaign's closing days, which were consumed by the candidacy of the other Dan Sullivan. The New York Times reported in late October, based on interviews, text messages and documents prepared for a potential lawsuit, that people connected to Peltola's campaign and national Democrats had allegedly helped recruit Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. into the race. The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee has denied involvement. Two days before the election, the senator told CNN's State of the Union that Peltola had misled voters about her campaign's role in recruiting the Petersburg candidate. "She got caught lying, and she's still lying to the Alaskan people, the media, to all of us," he said. Peltola has rejected all allegations. "I am not interested in tricking voters," she has said. The Justice Department sued to block certification if Sullivan lost but would have won had every vote for Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. gone to him instead, pending an investigation into whether those voters meant to choose the senator. A federal judge dismissed the suit on November 1, and the department has appealed. President Donald Trump has since written that votes for "the Fake Dan Sullivan" should be given to the senator, a demand analysts told Newsweek runs counter to Alaska's ranked-choice system. On election night, as early returns came in, Sullivan sounded a different note. "Lower 48 blue wave. But we're different," he told supporters. When Will the Alaska Senate Race Be Called? Key Dates Ahead The week ahead is crowded. Ballots mailed from overseas can arrive through Wednesday. The Division of Elections has scheduled its final count of absentee and questioned ballots, and the ranked-choice tabulation, for the same day. It targets certification for November 25. The campaign's posture has been consistent, if spare. Last Wednesday, Adams said the campaign would "look forward to a complete and accurate count." Monday's post opened with the same phrase, then carried it through to certification and, for the first time, put a date on the campaign's next move. It did not say what that move will be: a concession, a challenge or a decision to wait for certification. Newsweek has reached out to the Sullivan and Peltola campaigns for comment. Alaska has been counting for nearly two weeks. Sullivan's campaign, quiet for nearly as long, now says it will have "more to say by the end of this week." Newsweek’s reporters and editors used Martyn, our AI assistant, to produce this story. Learn more about Martyn here. Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Steven Frank and Edward T. Cummins
news.summary: Dan Sullivan’s campaign breaks its silence in the uncalled Alaska Senate race against Mary Peltola, with a promise for this week.
news.author: Lars Hanson

news.title: PM Modi Arrives In Manila For ASEAN-India And East Asia Summits As Quad Meeting With Trump Expected On Sidelines
news.text: New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was accorded a warm welcome by members of the Indian diaspora as his aircraft touched down in Manila at 4.50 pm local time (2.20 pm IST). The prime minister’s visit comes ahead of the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, both scheduled to take place on Tuesday. The Quad summit is also expected to be held on the sidelines of these meetings, with US President Donald Trump scheduled to arrive in Manila on Tuesday evening. The meeting would be the first Quad summit under Trump’s second term. In a statement issued before his arrival in Manila, Modi said India’s relationship with ASEAN countries was at the heart of its Act East Policy and occupied a central place in its MAHASAGAR vision.“Our ties, rooted in centuries of civilisational exchanges, have grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-topeople relations,” he said.India is looking to build a mutually beneficial trade partnership with the 11-member ASEAN grouping while expanding cooperation with East Asian countries in areas such as digital connectivity, submarine cable networks and defence.PM Narendra Modi To Visit Brussels In Mid-December To Sign India-EU Free Trade Agreement, Says EU Ambassador Jean-Eric Paquet India and ASEAN have designated 2026 as the Year of Maritime Cooperation. Officials in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said the summit would provide an opportunity to strengthen collaboration in maritime security, maritime safety, connectivity and the blue economy.Secretary (East) Rudrendra Tandon said India firmly believed that a strong strategic relationship with ASEAN member states, both collectively and individually, was in the interests of both sides.“We in India strongly believe that as an Indian Ocean country that abuts this very important Southeast Asian maritime zone, a strong strategic relationship with the ASEAN member states, as a collective as well as individually, is good for both of us. It will make us more resilient to handle the very rapid geopolitical changes that are taking place around us and will also, I think, contribute to peace and stability in Asia as a whole,” he said.'We Are Very Proud' Indian Diaspora Celebrates PM Modi's Arrival In Philippines For ASEAN Summit Maritime cooperation has also been a key priority for the Philippines. Addressing the opening plenary of the ASEAN Summit, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. called for an “effective and substantive Code of Conduct” in the South China Sea in accordance with international law.Modi will also attend the East Asia Summit following the ASEAN-India Summit on Tuesday. The East Asia Summit is the premier leaders-led forum in the Indo-Pacific. Since its inception in 2005, it has played a significant role in shaping the strategic and geopolitical landscape of East Asia.Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping have not confirmed their attendance at the East Asia Summit. They are scheduled to meet Trump on Thursday in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

news.title: Elon Musk expected to accompany Trump on China visit; Iran on agenda for trilateral talks with Xi, Putin
news.text: Washington DC Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk is expected to accompany US President Donald Trump on his Asia tour, while discussions on Iran are likely to feature in the US President's upcoming trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen. According to CBS News, a senior White House official confirmed that Musk would be part of the presidential delegation travelling to Asia but would not participate in the meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin scheduled for Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. The issue of Iran is expected to feature in the trilateral discussions, with a senior US official indicating that Trump intends to raise the matter with the Chinese and Russian leaders. "I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin," the senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters, according to CBS News. The meeting, which would mark the first gathering between the three leaders, is expected to focus primarily on reducing the proliferation of nuclear weapons, even as the ongoing conflicts in Iran and Ukraine remain among the broader geopolitical concerns. Speaking to reporters before departing for his Asia tour on Monday, Trump said the leaders would discuss denuclearisation, describing it as a "tough subject," alongside developments concerning Iran and Ukraine. However, a US official had indicated over the weekend that the Russia-Ukraine conflict was not expected to feature in the discussions. Trump's Asia tour comes amid continuing geopolitical tensions and Washington's efforts to engage Beijing and Moscow on nuclear arms control and international security issues. The US President is scheduled to first visit the Philippines to participate in the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and hold discussions with regional leaders. On Tuesday, Trump is expected to meet leaders of India, Japan and Australia under the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad), marking the first in-person Quad leaders' summit in two years and the first during his current presidential term. The discussions are expected to focus on regional security and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific. Trump is also scheduled to sign a trade agreement with Thailand and attend a dinner with Southeast Asian leaders.On Wednesday, Trump will attend a state visit and luncheon banquet hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at the presidential palace before departing for Shenzhen, China. During his China visit, Trump is expected to participate in the APEC summit and hold bilateral discussions with Xi before joining the Chinese and Russian presidents for the trilateral meeting. Trump also indicated the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his Asia tour, although no formal meeting has been confirmed. "We're making a big trip. We're going to the Philippines, a big meeting mostly on economics, but a lot of other things will be discussed... And then we go to China, and we'll be with President Xi. He was here a month ago. And we're also going to meet with President Putin, and we may meet with Kim Jong Un, also," Trump told reporters before boarding Marine One at the White House. Meanwhile, senior members of the Trump administration, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, are also accompanying the President. Trump's visit comes against the backdrop of broader US-China trade and technology tensions, including concerns surrounding Nvidia's advanced semiconductor exports to China. However, White House officials said the issue was not expected to dominate discussions during the visit.The Asia tour is expected to conclude after Trump's engagements in China, with the US President also referring to the upcoming G20 summit in Miami in December as another major diplomatic engagement.
news.summary: A senior White House official confirmed that Musk would be part of the presidential delegation travelling to Asia but would not participate in the meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin
